paragraphs: A base figure is not meant to be looked at. It is meant to be dressed, rigged, sculpted over or used as the thing a garment hangs on, which is why an A pose and a clean topology matter more than any detail on the surface.

The figure is deliberately light at 21,266 polygons and 18,216 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification so it moves cleanly between engines. It is supplied in an A pose, ready for your own rig.
At $149 it suits character development and retopology work, garment and apparel visualisation, anatomy reference, game pipelines and previsualisation. On sale since 2025.

Weightlessness has a posture, and it is not standing. Limbs drift into a neutral crouch, nothing bears load, and the body hangs at whatever angle it was left at. A floating astronaut only reads as convincing when the pose admits that there is no down.

The figure holds 24,257 polygons and 24,922 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, kept light for scenes where the astronaut is one element among many. The visor is transparent rather than mirrored, so the head remains visible. Built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits space programme visualisation, education and museum work, advertising and editorial illustration, film and game environments. On sale since 2025.

The Catalina was slow, ugly and almost impossible to shoot down by boredom alone, because it stayed airborne for a day at a time. It found submarines, rescued downed crews and mapped coastlines, doing the unglamorous work of the war from a hull that could land on water.

The airframe holds 371,634 polygons and 388,788 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 66 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits aviation history and documentary work, museum and exhibition material, flight simulation, film and game environments. On sale since 2017.

The Transit has been the default working van in Britain for so long that its name became the generic term. A 2020 body is the modern shape of that: taller, more aerodynamic and full of driver aids, but doing the same job it has done since the sixties.

The model holds 211,313 polygons and 241,978 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 17 maps all at 4096x4096. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits street and architectural visualisation, fleet and livery mockups, logistics presentation, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2020.

A frog at rest is a coiled spring. The back legs are folded under a body that looks too small for them, and everything about the silhouette is explained the moment the animal jumps. Posing one convincingly means understanding that fold.

This build is prepared for Cinema 4D and ships rigged, so it opens as a native scene rather than an import. Native rigged builds for Maya and for Modo are offered separately, and it is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits nature and wildlife visualisation, education and museum work, animation and game assets, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

Science fiction suits diverge from real ones in one specific way: they are designed to be recognisable in silhouette. Hard panels, a defined helmet line and a visor that reads as a face substitute, because a character whose expression is hidden still has to carry a scene.
The figure holds 24,257 polygons and 24,922 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, light enough for real time use and crowd scenes. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 it suits science fiction film and animation, game characters, concept art, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

Geothermal power is the only generation method that treats the planet itself as the boiler. Steam comes up, drives a turbine, condenses and goes back down, and the plant on the surface is mostly pipework arranged around that loop, with the cooling towers doing the visible work.

The scene holds 199,870 polygons and 220,362 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 31 maps, 4 at 8192x8192 and 7 at 4096x4096, the remainder smaller. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $149 it suits energy and infrastructure visualisation, renewable power presentation, education and documentary work, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2018.

The ogre is what a fairy tale invents when it needs a threat that is stupid rather than cunning. Bulk over the shoulders, a low forehead, hands too big for tools: aggression posed into the silhouette, so the creature reads before any animation starts.
The model is deliberately light at 19,746 polygons and 9,885 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, suited to real time use and crowd scenes, and carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits game creatures, fantasy film and animation, tabletop and card art, concept illustration and book covers. On sale since 2023.

A continuous miner cuts and loads in one motion, which is what removed the blasting cycle from underground coal and rock work. The drum of picks at the front does the cutting, the gathering arms sweep the spoil back, and the whole machine crawls forward into the face it just made.
The model holds 656,639 polygons and 671,520 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, in a used and worn condition rather than factory finish, and carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits mining and resources visualisation, heavy equipment marketing, training and safety material, documentary and film, and game environments. On sale since 2026.

The palletized load system solved a logistics problem rather than a combat one: a truck that loads and unloads its own flatrack without a crane or a forklift, so supplies can be dropped anywhere a vehicle can reach. Most of what an army moves, moves this way.
The vehicle holds 812,355 polygons and 863,740 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, finished in camouflage and in used condition. It carries StemCell certification.
At $149 it suits military logistics visualisation, defence presentation, documentary and film, simulation, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A goalie's kit is not clothing, it is equipment with a person inside. Leg pads sized to close the gap between the posts, a blocker on one hand and a catching glove on the other, a mask built to take a puck at full speed. Every piece exists because of a specific injury someone once had.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the protective pieces in blue as static items. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $149 the set suits sports visualisation and equipment marketing, game characters, broadcast and editorial graphics, advertising and film previsualisation. On sale since 2020.

Giving a robot a thoughtful pose is a deliberate provocation. Weight on one leg, head slightly turned, a stance borrowed from classical sculpture rather than from machinery: it is a figure designed to make the viewer wonder what it is doing rather than what it is for.
The model holds 229,704 polygons and 170,078 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification for use across engines and renderers.
At $149 it suits technology and AI visualisation, editorial and conceptual illustration, advertising, science fiction film, game characters and exhibition work. On sale since 2023.

The hyena is built at an angle, front legs longer than the back, which gives it that sloped, loping profile and an endurance that outlasts almost anything it follows. It is a better hunter than its reputation allows, and the reputation is mostly bad press from people who watched it scavenge.

The animal is deliberately light at 11,344 polygons and 11,890 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification. The library also holds running and walking poses and a rigged build.
At $149 it suits wildlife and nature visualisation, documentary and education work, game creatures, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

Dakar trucks are the strangest class in motorsport: lorries jumping dunes at speeds that would frighten a rally car, with a crew of three and a spare wheel that takes two of them to lift. KAMAZ has won the category so often that the blue trucks are what most people picture when the race is mentioned.

The model holds 260,362 polygons and 293,205 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 14 maps, 13 at 4096x4096 and one at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $149 it suits motorsport visualisation and broadcast graphics, advertising, off road and vehicle presentation, film and game environments. On sale since 2018.
